When optimal blood glucose levels are not being maintained

use of insulin, insulin analogs, metformin, and glyburide dur-

screening for the development of diabetes or prediabetes at 
least every 3 years (ADA, 2014b).
Other Types of Diabetes
This category includes diabetes associated with specific genetic 
syndromes (such as maturity-onset diabetes of youth), genetic 
defects in insulin action, diseases of the exocrine pancreas (such 
as cystic fibrosis), endocrinopathies, (such as acromegly or 
Cushing’s syndrome), drug or chemical induced (such as in the 
treatment of HIV/AIDS or after organ transplantation), infec-
tions, and other illnesses. Such types of diabetes may account 
for 1% to 5% of all diagnosed cases of diabetes (ADA, 2014a).
SCREENING AND DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA
Screening for Diabetes
Screening for diabetes should be considered in all adults who 
are overweight (body mass index [BMI] 25 kg/m2) and who 
have one or more additional risk factors for T2DM listed below.

45 years. If tests are normal, testing should be done at 3-year
